question: Aditya-L1 primarily studies which layer of the Sun?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Corona**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aditya-L1 Mission:** The **Aditya-L1** is India's first solar mission, developed by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO).** It is designed to study the **Sun**, especially its outermost layer, the **Corona.**
 
• The **Corona** is the Sun's outermost layer, extending millions of kilometers into space. It is highly significant because of its influence on space weather and its role in understanding solar phenomena.
 
• Aditya-L1 is positioned at the **Lagrange Point 1 (L1)**, approximately 1.5 million kilometers from Earth. This location allows uninterrupted observation of the Sun without the interference of Earth's shadow.
 
• The **primary objectives** of Aditya-L1 include studying the dynamics of the Corona, solar magnetic fields, solar wind, and coronal mass ejections (CMEs). These phenomena are crucial for understanding how solar activities impact Earth.
 
• The mission is equipped with **seven payloads**, including instruments like the Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC), Solar Ultraviolet Imaging Telescope (SUIT), and Plasma Analyser Package for Aditya (PAPA), dedicated to studying various aspects of the Corona and solar atmosphere.
 
• The study of the Corona is essential because it is the source of **solar wind** and space weather effects that influence satellite communications, GPS systems, and even power grids on Earth. Hence, understanding it is vital for technological safety.
 
• **Aditya-L1** also aims to investigate why the Corona is significantly hotter than the Sun's surface (**photosphere**) despite being farther away from the Sun's core. This is a long-standing mystery in astrophysics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Corona:**

 
 
• The Corona is a **plasma layer** that emits X-rays and ultraviolet radiation. It is visible during a total solar eclipse as a glowing halo around the Sun.
 
• It has a temperature of up to **millions of degrees Kelvin**, much higher than the Sun's surface, which is approximately **5,500 degrees Celsius.** Scientists aim to decode this temperature anomaly.
 
 
 
• **Lagrange Point 1 (L1):**
 
 
• The Lagrange Point 1 is a gravitationally stable point between the Sun and Earth, allowing constant observation of the Sun without interruptions.
 
• It is located approximately **1.5 million kilometers** from Earth, making it an ideal location for solar observation missions like Aditya-L1.
 
 
 
• **Payloads of Aditya-L1:**
 
 
• The Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (**VELC**) will study the Corona's magnetic field and structures.
 
• The Solar Ultraviolet Imaging Telescope (**SUIT**) observes the Sun's ultraviolet radiation and chromosphere.
 
• The Plasma Analyser Package for Aditya (**PAPA**) measures solar wind and energetic particles in the Corona.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Aditya-L1:**

 
 
• Aditya-L1 is India's first dedicated solar mission, marking a milestone in **solar research** and space exploration.
 
• The mission's findings will help improve predictions of **space weather**, safeguarding technological infrastructure and astronauts during space missions.
 
 
 
• **Features of the Corona:**
 
 
• The Corona plays a critical role in producing **solar wind**, a stream of charged particles that affect Earth's magnetosphere and technology systems.
 
• Understanding phenomena like coronal mass ejections (**CMEs**) is essential to predict and mitigate their impact on Earth's technological systems.
